selector.rationale: The presence of numerous eosinophils and superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation, along with the lack of response to oral terbinafine, supports the diagnosis of drug-induced eosinophilic dermatitis.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
rejected.why: While eosinophils are present, the clinical presentation and biopsy findings are more consistent with drug-induced eosinophilic dermatitis.

rejected.label: Immune-related adverse event (irAE) of immunotherapy
rejected.why: This is a broad category and not a specific diagnosis, with no unique findings to support it over other options.

rejected.label: Ipilimumab-induced dermatitis
rejected.why: While the patient is on ipilimumab, the findings are more consistent with drug-induced eosinophilic dermatitis, which can be caused by multiple medications, including pembrolizumab and ipilimumab.
